issues.title: Undefined identifier True used instead
issues.description: The rule requires all TypeScript code to compile successfully with strict mode enabled. The code uses `True` (Python-style boolean) which is not a valid JavaScript/TypeScript identifier, causing a compilation error.
issues.rule_name: TypeScript Files Must Follow Strict TypeScript Configuration

issues.title: JSON schema not normalized before storage
issues.description: In the handleJSONSchemaChange callback, the code stores the raw user input value directly instead of the normalized JSON.stringify(v, null, 2) version. This means that if a user enters compact JSON like {"type":"object"}, it will be stored as-is rather than being formatted consistently. This breaks the intended behavior where all JSON schemas should be stored in a standardized pretty-printed format with 2-space indentation. When the schema is later retrieved and displayed, it may have inconsistent formatting, and downstream consumers expecting normalized JSON may encounter issues.

issues.title: JSON schema cleared for all variable types, not just jsonObject
issues.description: The payloadToSave logic removes the json_schema field whenever isSchemaEmpty is true, regardless of the variable type. The original code correctly checked `tempPayload.type === InputVarType.jsonObject && isSchemaEmpty`. By removing the type check, if a user switches from jsonObject type to another type (like textInput) and the schema happens to be empty, the json_schema field gets cleared even though it should be preserved during the transition. This causes data loss when users change variable types back and forth.

issues.title: JSON schema validation uses non-normalized value
issues.description: The validation logic for jsonObject type validates jsonSchemaValue instead of normalizedJsonSchema. This is problematic because normalizedJsonSchema is computed earlier and correctly handles the case where an empty schema should be undefined. By validating jsonSchemaValue directly, the code validates the raw tempPayload value instead of the cleaned version. This inconsistency means that validation may pass but the wrong data could be saved, or validation may fail when it should succeed if the schema is empty but not yet normalized.

issues.title: Dead store / unused variable `normalizedJsonSchema`
issues.description: SonarJS no-dead-store is enforced at error level. `normalizedJsonSchema` is assigned but never used afterwards, making it a dead store and a lint violation.
issues.rule_name: Frontend ESLint Sonarjs Rules Must Be Followed

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #30412 - fix(web): enable JSON_OBJECT type support in console UI

structured_output.summary:
This PR exposes the `JSON_OBJECT` input type in the chatflow/workflow variable editor by removing the hard-coded `isSupportJSON = false` gate. It also changes how the JSON Schema is handled: the editor now shows and stores the full schema instead of only its `properties`, the schema's top-level `type` must be `"object"`, and an empty editor clears `json_schema`. The placeholder is updated to match, and new i18n keys cover the two error messages across all locales.

The direction is right. The backend (`api/core/app/app_config/entities.py`) already accepts any Draft7 schema, so storing the user's schema verbatim removes the old wrap-and-unwrap mapping. However, `handleJSONSchemaChange` contains `return True`, which is not a valid TypeScript/JavaScript literal and will fail type-checking and lint. The PR also has a silent-data-loss path: invalid JSON typed into the editor is discarded on Save without any message, and no tests cover the new validation.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The `return True` typo (capital T, undefined identifier) breaks `tsc`/lint, and it only "works" at runtime because the ReferenceError is swallowed by the surrounding `catch`. Beyond that, Save can silently persist the last valid schema while the editor shows invalid JSON, and none of the new validation logic has tests even though the checklist says it does. These should be fixed before merge; the rest of the design is sound.

architecture.overview:
Dify stores app and workflow input variables as `InputVar` objects. Their `json_schema` field is a JSON string, and the backend validates it with `Draft7Validator.check_schema` in `VariableEntity.validate_json_schema`. In the web console, `ConfigModal` in `config-var/config-modal/index.tsx` edits one variable at a time. Before this PR the `JSON_OBJECT` option was hidden behind a hard-coded `isSupportJSON = false`. The editor also wrapped whatever the user typed as `properties` inside a generated object schema.

The PR removes the feature gate, so `jsonObject` is offered for chatflow and workflow apps (basic apps are still excluded by `isBasicApp`). The editor now displays and stores the whole schema verbatim. The save path only checks that the top-level `type` is `"object"`, and clears `json_schema` when the editor is empty. The placeholder in `config.ts` is updated to the full-schema shape.
steps: Entry point: the user picks the `JSON` type in `ConfigModal`'s `selectOptions`, which is now shown whenever `!isBasicApp`.

Editing: `CodeEditor` calls `handleJSONSchemaChange`. Valid JSON is written to `tempPayload.json_schema` as-is, empty input clears it, and invalid input is ignored, which leaves the last valid value in state. The `return True` on the valid path is a bug.
Display: `jsonSchemaStr` re-serializes the stored schema with `JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(...), null, 2)` so the editor shows the full object, not just `properties`.

Save: `handleConfirm` computes `payloadToSave`, dropping `json_schema` when it is empty. For `jsonObject` it parses the stored string and requires `type === 'object'`, showing a translated toast otherwise. This check runs on the last valid state, not on what is currently in the editor.

Backend: the saved string is later validated by `VariableEntity.validate_json_schema` in `api/core/app/app_config/entities.py`. This PR does not change the backend, so the two layers agree on the Draft7 contract.

diagrams.description: How a JSON Schema typed in the console moves from the editor through the modal state and save check to the backend validator.

findings.title: `return True` is an undefined identifier that breaks type-check and lint
findings.fixPrompt: In `web/app/components/app/configuration/config-var/config-modal/index.tsx`, `handleJSONSchemaChange` (around line 139) has `return True`, which is an undefined identifier. It should be `true`. Better still, remove the `return` value if the `CodeEditor` onChange callback does not use it, and drop the unused `const v = JSON.parse(value)` binding, or use `JSON.parse(value)` as a plain validity check. Check the `CodeEditor` onChange type before choosing. Confirm the file type-checks and lints.

findings.title: Save silently persists the last valid schema when the editor holds invalid JSON
findings.fixPrompt: In `web/app/components/app/configuration/config-var/config-modal/index.tsx`, `handleJSONSchemaChange` (around lines 130-145) returns early on invalid JSON without recording it, so `tempPayload.json_schema` keeps the last valid value. `handleConfirm` (around lines 247-330) then saves that stale schema without warning when the user clicks Save with invalid text in the editor. Keep track of the raw editor text, or a validity flag, in component state. In `handleConfirm`, when the current text is not valid JSON, show the existing `variableConfig.errorMsg.jsonSchemaInvalid` toast and return, so the stale schema is not saved. Keep the existing empty-schema handling.

findings.title: No tests cover the new JSON schema behavior
findings.body:
The PR checklist says a test was added for each change, but the diff contains no spec files. The `config-modal` directory has no spec file either (`config.ts`, `field.tsx`, `index.tsx`, `type-select.tsx` only). The new branches are untested: the empty-schema clearing, the `type !== 'object'` toast, the invalid-JSON toast in `handleConfirm`, and the `payloadToSave` stripping of `json_schema`.

A small `index.spec.tsx` that renders `ConfigModal` with a `jsonObject` payload would cover these. It would also have caught the `return True` typo, since lint and type-check run over the file.
findings.fixPrompt: Add a Vitest/RTL spec next to `web/app/components/app/configuration/config-var/config-modal/index.tsx` (for example `index.spec.tsx`). Cover these cases: a jsonObject variable with a schema whose top-level type is not 'object' shows the `jsonSchemaMustBeObject` toast and does not call `onConfirm`; invalid JSON shows `jsonSchemaInvalid` and does not call `onConfirm`; a valid object schema calls `onConfirm` with the schema string unchanged; an empty editor calls `onConfirm` with `json_schema` undefined. Follow the mocking patterns of existing config-var specs in the repo. Assert on the `onConfirm` payload and toast calls, not on internal state.

findings.title: Unused `normalizedJsonSchema` variable
findings.body:
`normalizedJsonSchema` is computed in `handleConfirm` but never read. `payloadToSave` does the real work. The repo's unused-variable lint rule will flag this, and it is misleading because it looks like the value that gets saved.

::diff{file="web/app/components/app/configuration/config-var/config-modal/index.tsx" lines="249-260"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `web/app/components/app/configuration/config-var/config-modal/index.tsx` inside `handleConfirm` (around line 251), remove the unused `normalizedJsonSchema` constant. `payloadToSave` already handles the empty-schema case, so nothing else changes.

findings.title: `jsonObjectWrap` is now dead code
findings.body:
The only consumer of `jsonObjectWrap` was the old `handleJSONSchemaChange` wrapping logic, and the import was removed from `index.tsx`. Nothing else in `web/` imports it, so the export in `config.ts` can be deleted. This keeps the file focused on the new placeholder.

::diff{file="web/app/components/app/configuration/config-var/config-modal/config.ts" lines="1-6"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `web/app/components/app/configuration/config-var/config-modal/config.ts`, delete the now-unused `jsonObjectWrap` export (lines 1-6). Grep `web/` first to confirm there are no remaining imports, then leave `jsonConfigPlaceHolder` unchanged.

findings.title: Stored schema format now matches backend validation
findings.body:
Storing the schema verbatim, instead of wrapping the user's `properties`, lines up with `VariableEntity.validate_json_schema` in `api/core/app/app_config/entities.py`. That validator runs `Draft7Validator.check_schema` on the whole document, so the editor, the placeholder, and the backend now describe the same contract. Clearing the editor sends `undefined`, which removes `json_schema` from the payload. That is the right behavior for an optional field, and it avoids storing an empty string that would fail the backend parse.

The placeholder now shows a top-level `type: "object"` and `properties`, which makes the constraint visible to users before they hit the toast.

findings.title: Translations added for all supported locales
findings.body: Both new `variableConfig.errorMsg.jsonSchemaInvalid` and `variableConfig.errorMsg.jsonSchemaMustBeObject` keys are added to every `web/i18n/*/app-debug.json`. They are placed alphabetically next to the existing `errorMsg` keys. The code uses `t(...)` with the same namespace as the surrounding messages, so no key is missing at runtime.
